title: SSO session orchestration: JIT provisioning timing, MFA signal routing, logout propagation, and reauth windows
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Design and implement an orchestration layer for SSO session lifecycle that reconciles JIT user provisioning timing with MFA expectations, ensures cross-service logout propagation, and enforces re-auth (step-up) windows tied to RBAC v2 constraints and audit logging requirements. This ticket covers spec, API changes, runtime checks, and audit-event schema for session lifecycle events originating from SAML/SSO identity providers.
acceptance_criteria: JIT provisioning can be delayed up to a configurable grace window while allowing a session to be established for immediate MVP flows (default 30s), with deterministic behavior documented
MFA expectations (assertions/hints) in SAML Response are translated into session attributes that influence step-up prompts and are recorded in audit logs
Admin-initiated logout and IdP-initiated single logout (SLO) propagate to Dedicated and Private deployments within SLA (configurable), and corresponding tokens/kv-caches are invalidated
Re-auth policy windows (short/medium/long) can be bound to RBAC v2 roles and enforced at request time with clear fallback when IdP is unavailable
Audit events emitted for session create/augment/revoke/reauth include correlation_id, idp_flow_id, provision_state, mfa_hint, and affected_roles and conform to audit schema v2
technical_notes: We currently accept SAML assertions and perform immediate create-user-on-first-auth (JIT). In high-scale bursts this leads to racing between JIT write to user DB and initial token issuance. Introduce a 'provisional session' state allowing a short-lived token that is exchangeable for a full session once provisioning completes
Provisional session must be tagged in audit log with provision_state=provisional and linked via idp_flow_id to the eventual full session event

MFA signals: Some IdPs provide 'AuthnContext' or 'AuthnContextClassRef' indicating MFA level. Map these to internal mfa_level enum (none, single_factor, multi_factor). This drives whether step-up should be forced for sensitive routes

Logout propagation: For IdP SLO requests we must call internal revoke endpoints for runtime, clear KV-caches for that user on serving runtime nodes, and publish a logout event to the global change stream for Dedicated/Private control planes

Reauth windows: Implement configurable per-role reauth_ttl (seconds) in RBAC v2 backplane. At request time, the session's last_auth_time is compared. If stale, trigger step-up flow. Provide graceful offline fallback using cached step-up tokens with short TTL
Audit schema additions: add fields correlation_id, idp_flow_id, provision_state, mfa_hint, initiated_by (user|idp|admin|system), affected_resources (list string), and prior_session_id
implementation_plan: Spec review with Security and SSO teams (this ticket)
Add provisional session state to session-service and define exchange API: POST /sessions/exchange-provisional -> full session
Extend SAML handler to emit idp_flow_id and mfa_hint parsed from assertion attributes
Implement RBAC v2 hook to evaluate reauth_ttl and return step-up requirement at policy-eval time
Add logout propagation paths: internal revoke endpoint, serving runtime KV cache invalidation job, and publish to global change stream
Add audit-event emission at each transition with new audit schema fields
Create e2e tests and simulate IdP delays, IdP-initiated SLO, admin revoke and verify audit events and token invalidation
testing_plan: Unit tests for provisional session lifecycle and exchange API
Integration tests: simulate SAML response with delayed user DB write (introduce artificial latency) and assert provisional->full transition
Load test: burst of first-time SSO logins to validate no DB deadlocks and acceptable latency for exchange flow
Chaos test: simulate IdP unavailable during step-up and confirm offline fallback path (cached step-up tokens) behaves as expected
Security tests: verify MFA hints cannot be forged by client; validate signature verification path and assertion attribute parsing
Audit verification: pipeline tests ensure new audit fields appear in downstream SIEM and correlate to request traces
rollout_plan: Feature gate behind 'sso-session-orchestration' flag in staging and canary clusters
Start with non-critical customers in Dedicated stage for two weeks, monitor logout success and audit delivery rates
Enable for more customers after validation; set default provisional window to 30s, allow per-org override via console
Monitor key KPIs: percent of provisional sessions, average provisional exchange latency, SLO for logout propagation (target <5s for hosted, <30s for Dedicated), audit delivery latency
comments: 2025-11-12 Aisha Kumar: Kickoff — drafted initial spec for orchestration to address race conditions during JIT provisioning and to better capture MFA signals for downstream step-up decisions.

2025-11-13 Marco Reyes: Implementor note — will add provisional session state to existing session-service; need to coordinate schema changes with audit team. Blocking question: should provisional tokens be usable for write operations? Recommend read-only until full provisioning completes.

2025-11-14 Priya Nair (Security): Security review requested. Concern: provisional session could be abused if allowed to access sensitive APIs. Require read-only enforcement and audit tagging. Also require rate limit on provisional exchanges to avoid amplification attacks.
2025-11-15 Design review (Liam Cho): UX for admin console needs to expose 'pending provision' users and let admins trigger finalize or rollback. Created follow-up PM/design ticket if needed.

2025-11-17 Marco Reyes: PR opened for session-service changes: github.com/redwood/platform/pull/11893. Includes provisional state machine and new exchange endpoint. Unit tests included. Needs integration test infra allocation.
2025-11-18 Aisha Kumar: Updated spec to include audit schema additions and reauth_ttl binding to RBAC v2. Marking security_review_required=true per Priya's request. Moving to In Progress.
